title: Reject damaged ZIP entries and TAR headers
goal: Handle ZIP CRC and TAR header-checksum failures at the complete read boundary, without treating checksums as authentication.

selectionNotes: Handle ZIP CRC and TAR header-checksum failures at the complete read boundary, without treating checksums as authentication. Desktop/server examples; inspect complete constraints before use.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: This edition uses or relies on .NET 11 framework APIs/behaviour; .NET 10 is comparison-only.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 comparison with its matching SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical .NET 11 project selects its supported C# 15 default.

platforms: Desktop/server .NET platforms; authoring execution recorded on Windows. Browser/WASI excluded from these samples.
prerequisites: Use a net11.0 console project with LangVersion=15.0, implicit usings and the namespaces stated in the complete recipe. No additional package, workload, account or provider is required.
constraints: ZIP CRC validation requires reading an entry through EOF; opening an archive or reading only a prefix is insufficient. TAR validates headers, not a cryptographic digest of entry payloads. CRC32 and TAR checksums detect damage and do not establish authenticity or resist deliberate tampering. Dispose readers and entry streams after failure. Extraction is not transactional; validate into staging before promoting output. Truncated/structurally invalid archives can fail earlier and may raise other documented I/O errors. No disable-validation switch is recommended. These bounded byte-array examples are not safe arbitrary-size ingestion: separately limit entry counts, expanded bytes, paths and links for untrusted input.
stabilityLimitations: Verified with SDK 11.0.100-rc.2.26504.105; RC2 execution is not GA verification.

sources.title: Official archive integrity, access and encryption implementation
Official TAR checksum and sparse-header reader

evidence.scope: Actual .NET 10 Windows compilation/execution: plain ZIP access/replacement, stored-CRC and TAR-header corruption acceptance baseline, four TAR formats and raw sparse body. Encryption is explicitly unavailable and its stub is tested. No mocks, cross-compilation or GA proof.

Original Stored ZIP payload bytes are flipped while preserving recorded CRCs; RC2 rejects the full read and .NET 10 returns changed bytes. A valid Ustar header name is changed without recomputing its checksum; RC2 rejects it while .NET 10 accepts it. Actual Windows compilation/execution; no mocks, cross-compilation or GA proof.

humanProof.scope: Bounded desktop/server archive and codec checks run locally without external providers or UI. No extra native/device or external-tool interoperability claim.
